short: The Lighthouse of Alexandria, or Pharos, was a towering Hellenistic structure that guided ships into the bustling Egyptian harbour.
full:
Built around 280 BCE by the Ptolemaic Kingdom on the small island of Pharos, the Lighthouse of Alexandria was an unprecedented feat of maritime engineering. Estimated to be over 100 metres tall, it was one of the tallest man-made structures in the world for many centuries, constructed in three tiers: a square base, an octagonal middle, and a circular top.

A mirror reflected sunlight during the day, while a large fire burned at night, projecting a beam visible for dozens of miles to guide ships safely through the treacherous coastline. The Pharos not only facilitated Alexandria's immense trade wealth but also became the architectural archetype for all subsequent lighthouses, with its name becoming the root word for 'lighthouse' in many modern languages.
